title: Part Two
html:
Nityananda and the vyuhas. Advaita Acharya and his family. Srivasa and "those called devotees." The sannyasi associates. Puri: Prataparudra, Sarvabhauma, Ramananda (verses 58–123)

Nityananda, "the devotee in essence"

58Since the part and the whole are not different, the original vyuha is the son of Shachi; Baladeva, the vyuha Sankarshana, is considered to be Vishvarupa.

59And by manifestation He is also called Nityananda Avadhuta. As Kali says to Dharma in the Gaura-chandrodaya:

60"His elder brother, who never took a wife, is Bhagavan Sankarshana Himself, Vishvarupa on earth; having passed His own splendour to the Puri-ishvara,1 He earlier took to the wandering life and disappeared."

61And also: "Nityananda Avadhuta, the splendour honoured [by Brahma and others], He who is Sankarshana."

62When this eternal Sri Vishvarupa disappeared, He, uniting with Nityananda Avadhuta, then remained in Him.

63"And so the divine Avadhuta, whose nature is Bala,2 always moving among the Vaishnavas, blazed with the splendour of a thousand suns" — so my father3 said as he danced.

64He who, by His own portion Shesha, is the bed, the clothing and the ornament of Vishnu and of Krishna, and in the form of the ornaments of His own body — bracelets and the rest — knows the hidden pastimes by the potency called lila.

65His two beloveds, Vasudha and Jahnavi — Sri Varuni and Revati, born in the line of Revata4 — are the daughters of the great-souled Sri Suryadasa, radiant as the sun, who is Kakudmi.5

66Some even in the age of Kali declare Sri Vasudha-devi [to be Ananga-manjari], and some say Jahnavi is Ananga-manjari. According to the former rule [of distinct manifestations], the saints hold both to be correct.

67The vyuha of Sankarshana, called the One who lies on the Ocean of Milk, became Virachandra, whose form is non-different from Chaitanya;

68into him, for the sake of the work, entered the brothers Nishatha and Ulmuka.6 Minaketana Ramadasa is the other Sankarshana, the original vyuha.

69The Ganga, born from the foot of Vishnu, was born under her own name as the daughter of Nityananda; her husband Madhava is King Shantanu.

70The third vyuha, Pradyumna, became the dear confidential friend (priya-narma-sakha) who assisted in the pastimes of Radha and Madhava in Vraja; non-different in body from Sri Chaitanya, he is Raghunandana.7

71The fourth vyuha, Aniruddha, is Vakreshvara Pandita, who gave joy to the Lord by his dancing, born of absorption in Krishna.

72It was he who spoke sweet words to the feet of Chaitanya: "O merciful One, give me a thousand singers."

73By a distinction of her own manifestation, Shashirekha8 entered into him. The appearance (avirbhava) of Gaurahari was in Nakula Brahmachari;

74and His entering (avesha) is likewise to be known in the Mishra named Pradyumna.9 Acharya Bhagavan, the lame one, is said to be a portion (kala) of Gaura.

75Gopinatha Acharya is to be known as Brahma, lord of the world, whom the knowers of the Tantras count in the Tantra among the nine vyuhas.

Advaita, "the incarnation of the devotee"

76Sadashiva, who in Vraja was a vyuha by being a form of empowerment (avesha), is Advaita Gosvami, whose form is non-different from Chaitanya.

77He, having assumed the body of a cowherd boy, danced in Vraja beside Krishna, as Bhairava says in the Shiva-tantra:

78"Once in the month of Karttika, at the great festival of lamps, Krishna, with Rama and the cowherd boys, danced with zeal.

79Seeing this, my guru,10 longing for the mood of a cowherd, began to dance with his Beloved, whirling like a wheel.

80By the grace of Sri Krishna Sadashiva became twofold: one there was Shiva himself, the other had the form of a cowherd boy."

81The friend of Mahadeva, Kubera, lord of the Guhyakas, is now Kubera Pandita, His [Advaita's] father, the "sky-clad."11

82Once Kubera, dear to Sri Shiva, on Kailasa, frequented by the Siddhas and Sadhyas, chanted the supreme mantra of Shiva.

83Then the merciful lord said, "Choose a boon," and Kubera chose: "Become my son."

84Entreated by him, Sadashiva, the lord of the gods and lord of boons, [said]: "In another birth I shall become your son."

85Having received this boon, he spent some time in austerity, and now, by the will of the Lord, for the sake of the work, he became the father of Advaita.

86Bhagavati Yogamaya is now His wife, descended in the form of Sita; and by her manifestation, the one named Shri.12

87His son is Achyutananda, dear to Krishna Chaitanya; it is known that he was the beloved disciple of Srimat Pandita Gosvami.13

88Some say that he was formerly Karttikeya; others, knowers of rasa, call him the gopi named Achyuta. Both are correct, since the two are united in one. But some say that Karttikeya is Krishna Mishra, by resemblance.14

89[Sita's maidservants] Nandini and Jangali are to be known as Jaya and Vijaya respectively.

Srivasa and "those called devotees"

90The wise Srivasa Pandita is the former sage Narada; the best of sages named Parvata, Narada's friend, is Sriman Rama Pandita, his younger brother.

91Murari Gupta is Hanuman; Angada is Sri Purandara; he who was called Sugriva is Govindananda.

92He who was formerly Vibhishana is considered to be Ramachandra Puri; therefore Gaurahari said: "The cause of this is not Rama." For the sake of the work, Jatila, Radhika's mother-in-law, entered into him; and therefore Mahaprabhu then reduced His alms and so on.15

93The son of the sage Richika, named Brahma, a great ascetic, was born together with Prahlada [in one person] and became the one called Haridasa.

94As the feet of Murari Gupta have said in the Chaitanya-charitamrita: the sage's son, bringing tulasi leaves in the morning

95unwashed, was cursed by his father and became a yavana; and he became Haridasa, endowed with supreme devotion.16

96The eight perfections, anima and the rest, who were formerly in Vrindavana, these same eight took the form of devotees and were born in Gauda, as follows:

97Ananta, Sukhananda, Govinda, Raghunatha, Krishnananda, Keshava, Sri Damodara and Raghava — in order, with the title "Puri" — are to be known as the eight perfections, anima and the rest.17

98The sons of Jayanti, established in celibacy and seeing all equally, the nine bhagavatas, who once declared the Bhagavata-samhita

99to King Janaka, have now become sannyasis and always sported with the Lord Gaurahari; namely:

100Sri Nrisimhananda Tirtha, Sri Satyananda Bharati, Sri Nrisimha, Chidananda and Jagannatha — the Tirthas;

101Vasudeva, called Tirtha; Sri Rama; Purushottama — [also] the Avadhuta named Garuda; and Sri Gopendra, called Ashrama.

102The nine treasures (nidhis) famed in the world — Padma, Shankha and the rest — were born here as the Lord's dear ones bearing the titles "nidhi," "ratna" and "garbha":

103Sri Srinidhi, Sri Garbha, Kaviratna, Sudhanidhi, Vidyanidhi, Gunanidhi, Ratnabahu, the foremost of brahmanas, Sriman Acharyaratna and Sri Ratnakara Pandita.

104Nilambara Chakravarti declared in an assembly the coming birth of Gaura; therefore he is called Garga.

105As the father of Sri Shachi he is considered to be the cowherd Sumukha; and she who was known in Vraja as Patala is to be known as his wife.

106Sri Devananda Pandita, the knower of the meaning of the Puranas, was formerly the sage Bhaguri, the pandit of Nanda's assembly.

107Kashinatha, Lokanatha, Srinatha and Ramanatha — these four, devotees endowed with knowledge, are without doubt Sanaka and the others.

108Since in all four names the word "natha" is heard, they are here called "the four Nathas," just like "the four Sanas."

109He who was Vedavyasa is now Vrindavana Dasa; for the sake of the work the friend Kusumapida also entered into him.

110Shuka, the son of Dvaipayana, became the Bhatta named Vallabha.18

111Acharya Sri Jagannatha and Gangadasa, dear to the Lord, were formerly Durvasa, dear to the gopis in Nidhuvana.

112The discerning should know Acharya Chandrashekhara as Chandra (the Moon); Sriman Uddhava Dasa too is an empowered incarnation (avesha-avatara) of the Moon.

113Therefore Chaitanya-Hari called him "the lord of the night." Srimad Vishveshvara Acharya was formerly Divakara (the Sun).

114He who was formerly Vishvakarma is now Bhaskara Thakura. The mendicant Vanamali was formerly the brahmana Sudama — and so, having obtained wealth in the company of the Lord, yet regarding it as sorrow, he wandered.19

115The two doorkeepers of Vaikuntha, Jaya and Vijaya, have now by their own will been born as Sri Jagannatha and Madhava.

116Pundarikaksha and Kumuda, famous in the realm of Vaikuntha, were born in Gauda as Govinda and Garuda, dear to the Lord.

117Garuda Pandita is the Garuda known of old from the scriptures. He who was formerly named Akrura is Gopinatha Simha, so some say; [others say that] Akrura is Keshava Bharati.

Puri

118Sri Paramananda Puri was formerly Uddhava. The great king Indradyumna, who once worshipped Jagannatha, has now been born as Prataparudra, equal to Indra.

119Sarvabhauma Bhattacharya was formerly the Lord of Speech (Brihaspati) in heaven.

120A certain dear confidential friend [of Krishna], Arjuna, and Arjuna the son of Pandu, uniting together, became Ramananda Raya, dear to the Lord.

121Therefore the skilful Ramananda day after day described to Gaurachandra the essence of devotion and love for Radha and Krishna.

122Some call him Lalita, but this is accepted by only a few: for Gaura said to Bhavananda: "You are Prithapati."20

123The best say that Arjuna, the son of Pandu, having united with the gopi Arjuniya, became Raya Ramananda.

✦

Translator's notes

Notes

  1. According to the commentators, the "Puri-ishvara" here is Paramananda Puri, not Ishvara Puri.
  2. Bala is Balarama.
  3. Shivananda Sena, the author's father.
  4. Varuni and Revati are the consorts of Balarama.
  5. Kakudmi is the father of Revati.
  6. Nishatha and Ulmuka are sons of Balarama.
  7. Raghunandana Thakura of Shrikhanda.
  8. Shashirekha is a gopi friend.
  9. Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita (Antya 2): Chaitanya manifested Himself in Nakula Brahmachari (avesha) and in Pradyumna (Nrisimhananda) Brahmachari (avirbhava).
  10. The words are Bhairava's: "my guru" is Sadashiva.
  11. "Sky-clad" (digambara), i.e. naked, is an epithet of Shiva (in the edition, of Mahadeva); the edition notes a variant reading vidambara ("the best of the learned").
  12. Advaita's second wife, Sri-devi.
  13. That is, of Gadadhara Pandita. Cf. the Advaita-prakasha, where Achyuta is the chief hero among Advaita's sons.
  14. Krishna Mishra is another son of Advaita; according to the Advaita-prakasha, he inherited the service of Madana-Gopala.
  15. Cf. Chaitanya-charitamrita (Antya 8): Ramachandra Puri's reproaches made Chaitanya cut down His food.
  16. Haridasa Thakura, born in a Muslim family.
  17. Anima ("becoming minute") and the rest are the eight mystic perfections of yoga.
  18. Vallabha Bhatta, founder of the Pushtimarga sampradaya.
  19. The edition interprets the line differently: wandering in the misery of poverty, he obtained in the Lord's company the wealth of prema.
  20. Bhavananda Raya, Ramananda's father; Prithapati, "the husband of Pritha," i.e. Pandu.
